summary: FPF Defense is developing SmartFlak, a counter-drone system built around Hammerhead, a low-cost autonomous kinetic interceptor meant to destroy Shahed-class one-way attack drones. Tectonic puts it at about 20 people, at the prototype stage. The Form D gives a New York address, and the press release says headquarters is relocating to West Palm Beach, Florida.
thesis: The press release describes an attack drone costing roughly $50,000 against missile interceptors that can cost millions. FPF answers with an interceptor the release says is engineered for U.S. mass production, built mostly from commercial off-the-shelf parts per Tectonic.
stage: Series Seed. The Form D filed 3 August 2026 shows a $10,000,000 equity offering sold in full to 4 investors, first sale 16 June 2026. Ondas's 10-Q says it bought Series Seed Preferred Stock on 17 June 2026 for $5.0 million. RSE Ventures co-led per the 24 July 2026 press release, amount undisclosed. The CEO told Tectonic the money gives 12 to 14 months of runway. No valuation is disclosed.

team.name: Christopher C. Miller
team.background: Chief Executive Officer and director. Per the press release, 27 years as a U.S. Army Green Beret, Director of the National Counterterrorism Center and Acting Secretary of Defense.

team.name: Grant Fox
team.background: Chief Operating Officer and director, signed the Form D as President. The press release cites U.S. Navy and Defense Innovation Unit experience. Tectonic calls him a co-founder.

team.name: Dr. Jeff Maas
team.background: Chief Technology Officer and former DARPA program manager per the press release. Tectonic calls him a co-founder. Not listed as a related person on the Form D.

team.name: Christian Sessoms
team.background: Chief Revenue Officer and fourth founder per the press release, a retired lieutenant colonel and career Army Special Forces officer. Executive officer on the Form D.

questions: The Form D shows 4 investors for $10,000,000 and Ondas's 10-Q accounts for $5.0 million. How much did RSE Ventures put in, and what rights did Ondas get?
Can you share government data from the May 2026 Camp Atterbury demo (2 of 3 targets hit, per the CEO) and the warhead evaluation scheduled for 28 July?
What is the bill of materials behind the roughly $30,000 unit cost today and the $15,000 to $20,000 full-rate target, and which parts are commercial off-the-shelf?
What are the terms with UAV Solutions in Baltimore, and how is the 1,000-a-month facility targeted for the end of 2027 funded if APFIT money does not arrive?
risks: The only performance evidence in the sources read is the CEO's own account (2 of 3 targets hit at Camp Atterbury in May 2026). No government or independent report was read.
The production plan is aggressive and partly unfunded: about 100 a month by November 2026, then 1,000 a month by end of 2027, against 12 to 14 months of runway.
Ondas supplied $5.0 million of the $10,000,000. The CEO says he expects close collaboration, possibly using Ondas production capacity. That could limit independence and options for a later investor.
unverified: Tectonic says testing is with OUSW-R&E under the T-Rex program, and Dual Use Investor describes an Army challenge. No government page naming FPF as a participant was read.
A search snippet gives Jeff Maas a 2018 to 2022 DARPA Strategic Technology Office tenure. No page opened states this or ties it to FPF's CTO.
It is not confirmed that the placeholder page at fpfdefense.com belongs to this company. The Wayback Machine lists captures from December 2021, before the 2025 incorporation.

announcement.what: The Wall Street Journal named FPF-Defense as the company Chris Miller now runs, a passing mention in a news article quoting him.
